column2: A DETAIL HOP THAT RE-FETCHES ITS OWN URL. Found 2026-10-25 by asking the whole tree a question first measured on one row.
It started at us-sf-311-open311-requests, whose open item was "measure a hostgate gap for the detail hops" - the row's own
notice reported them refused. The prior question is what the hop brought back. Open311 GeoReport v2 defines ONE representation
of a service request, so /requests/<id>.json is its single-resource form and not a deeper record: measured against four SF
cases chosen to differ (open/closed, with and without media_url, with and without status_notes) and against the other Open311
server in the tree (spot.brooklinema.gov), the list and detail representations are the same keys with identical values every
time. 48 of that row's 59 requests a run were buying nothing, and 1,026 of 1,074 records carried _detail_pending - a
disclosure that there was more behind the record, when there was not.
Asking it statically of all 627 rows that declare a detail_url - no requests at all - found 16 whose detail_url IS their url.
7 were removed with the Open311 work; the 9 below were each then MEASURED, one request, because "your detail_url is your own
endpoint" is NECESSARY for a worthless hop and not SUFFICIENT: a key naming a different id reaches a different document
through the same endpoint, which is a real thing to want.
make lint-sources fails the shape now (detail-self-hop). Its first predicate was OVER-BROAD and the tree said so at once -
110 findings, the first ones read being CKAN package_search beside package_show?id={v}, a correct hop in a defect bucket. On a
query URL the last "/"-segment is `package_search?rows=100` and its `100` passed a "looks like an id" test. Narrowed: the
query strings must be identical, the difference must be in the last PATH segment, and the url's own segment must be
digit-dense. A row that means it says so with a `detail-self-hop-ok: <reason>` marker, as page-offset-ok does.
verdict: SELF = every record's detail_key equals the id already in the url. NO-KEY = the key resolves on no record, so
hp_deepen() spends the budget and stamps _detail_error on every record - a disclosed failure to fetch a detail that does not
exist. WRONG-NS = the key resolves to an id from another namespace and the hop asks this endpoint for it (404s).
STILL OPEN, and deliberately not guessed at: all 9 ALSO carry one entity frozen into the url on a schedule, so each re-reads
one subject for ever and emits that one record's nested array. That is the shape repaired for both Open311 single-case rows
(`{q}` in the path plus interval 0, no collector relabel - registry_is_entity_pivot() reads interval 0, a non-`_` collector
and a `{q`-token). The path demonstrably takes an id, because the detail_url templated that exact position. What is NOT
settled per row is the entity shape gate (.want) and what the record set should be once the row is a pivot: array_path today
names a nested array of the one probe record, which is the probe's assumption and not the row's purpose. One reading of each
host, which is why it is listed rather than done.
